type: behaviour of table-record constructors (type 52 memory nodes at 0x40 stride with an embedded sub-object at +0x1C; type 92 scripts): they walk their whole blob = [entry, next table entry)
structure: Why inserting bytes anywhere inside the object span breaks the load: the enclosing table record grows and its constructor walks the inserted bytes
meaning: Run m3-…-1789299359139 (PlacementReference clone inserted at 0x457588, right after the type-52 table record 0x457548): the loader finished the level (21 402 records constructed, same as a healthy load) and the clone WAS constructed with the PlacementReference class pointer through P.next — the first clone ever instantiated — yet the load hung and the six tail root records (2 type-52 + 4 RHSValueStack) stayed raw. The clone body carries the exact signature of the type-52 constructor: class pointers written at clone+0x1C, +0x40 and +0x5C, and the texture tag "TFL8" at +0x44 rewritten as a refcount (0x54464C38 -> 0x040E4C38) — i.e. the type-52 record at 0x457548 saw its blob grow from 0x40 to 0xB0 and walked the clone as two of its own 0x40 nodes (node at clone+0x00 with embedded +0x1C, node at clone+0x40 with embedded +0x5C). Constructing the clone twice (reflection via P.next, then the stride walk) derailed the tail walk, the root records never constructed and the post-load init hung. General rule: every byte of the span belongs to some table record`s blob, and at least types 52 and 92 walk their blob positionally, so ANY insertion inside the span corrupts the enclosing record. Safe placements are therefore outside every walked blob: the section end (the last blob tolerated appended bytes intact in run m3-…-1789256664691) with reachability provided by a pointer from a constructed record.
